mnemonic: The hand 扌 closes on somebody who was already halfway out of the door. His mother, and not the police: つかまえる.
notes: 掴む つかむ is getting a grip on a thing. 捕まえる is catching something that was getting away from you.
sentence: 母が泥棒を捕まえました。
sentence_meaning: My mother caught the thief.

mnemonic: Early 早 and fast 速 at once, which is what you say when you are about to do the thing rather than promise it. The papers are on their way: さっそく.
sentence: では早速書類をお送りします。
sentence_meaning: Then I will send the documents immediately.

mnemonic: The belly 腹 with the polite お stuck on the front, and right now it is empty and saying so: おなか.
notes: 腹 はら is the blunter word for the same part. お腹 is what you actually say, and お腹が空く is being hungry.
sentence: お腹が空きました。
sentence_meaning: I'm hungry.

mnemonic: Sweep 掃 the place out and then take away 除 whatever the broom turned up. Every single day, apparently: そうじ.
sentence: 毎日、掃除します。
sentence_meaning: I clean everyday.

mnemonic: Stone 石 on the left and it gives you nothing whatever when you press on it. The bread is like that and still worth eating: かたい.
notes: 柔らかい やわらかい is the opposite. 固い and 堅い share the reading with different shades, and 硬い is the physically hard one.
sentence: このパンは硬いですが、美味しいです。
sentence_meaning: This bread is hard, but delicious.

mnemonic: The edge 際 where one thing meets the next, which is the moment to say what you have been holding onto. Now, then: さい.
notes: 時 とき is a time in general and 機会 きかい is a chance to act. 際 is formal and marks an occasion: この際, at this juncture.
sentence: この際はっきり言っておきます。
sentence_meaning: This is a good opportunity to speak frankly.

meaning: to give away, to let leak
mnemonic: Water gets through the roof that was put there to keep it out, and this time it was a secret and it was him: もらす.
notes: 漏れる もれる is a thing leaking by itself. 漏らす is somebody letting it out.
sentence: 秘密を漏らしたのは彼です。
sentence_meaning: He's the one who leaked the secret.

mnemonic: One face 面 of the thing turned toward you, with others you have not been shown. He had a side nobody expected: めん.
notes: 地面 じめん is the ground's surface. 面 alone is a surface, a side or an aspect, and it is also the mask worn in noh. 顔 かお is a person's face.
sentence: 彼の意外な面を見た。
sentence_meaning: I saw an unexpected side of him.

mnemonic: Not 不 full 満, which is precisely what being dissatisfied amounts to. The way he goes about it does not fill you: ふまん.
sentence: 私は彼のやり方には不満です。
sentence_meaning: I'm dissatisfied with his way of doing things.

mnemonic: The horse 馬 goes up on its back legs, and so did her face, and she could not get it back down again: おどろき.
sentence: 彼女は驚きを隠せませんでしたよ。
sentence_meaning: She was not able to conceal her surprise.

mnemonic: A banner 方 with people walking along behind it, going somewhere that takes days rather than hours. My sister does it often: たび.
notes: 旅行 りょこう is a trip as an arrangement, with dates and a hotel. 旅 is the journey itself, and it is the warmer word.
sentence: 姉はよく旅をします。
sentence_meaning: My big sister travels often.

mnemonic: Threads 糸 meeting 会 across a cloth, which is where pictures started before anybody had paint. That is a lovely one: え.
sentence: 素敵な絵ですね。
sentence_meaning: It's a beautiful drawing.

meaning: to pair up, to partner with
mnemonic: Two threads plaited into one so that neither of them goes anywhere alone now. Him and me, for this project: くむ.
sentence: このプロジェクトで私は彼と組んでいるんだ。
sentence_meaning: I am pairing up with him for this project.

mnemonic: Everything sinks 沈 and nobody says a word 黙, and it goes on long enough to become a thing in its own right: ちんもく.
notes: 無言 むごん is simply saying nothing. 沈黙 is a silence with weight, the sort that falls.
sentence: 彼はしばらく沈黙していた。
sentence_meaning: He was silent for a while.

mnemonic: Pulled tight 張 and held there until it aches, and after a day like that it is your shoulders: はる.
notes: Same reading as 春 はる, spring. 引っ張る ひっぱる is the tugging one, and this is being stretched taut.
sentence: 疲れて肩が張っています。
sentence_meaning: My shoulders are stiff with fatigue.

mnemonic: You tell 告 it plainly 白 with nothing at all held back. In Japan this is the moment two people start going out: こくはく.
notes: The word for confessing feelings. 告白する is the step that starts a relationship, rather than an admission in general.
sentence: 自分の思いを彼女に告白しました。
sentence_meaning: I confessed my feelings to her.

mnemonic: The tongue 舌 out and doing the work itself, and it was the dog, and it was your face: なめる.
notes: Also does looking down on somebody: 舐めるな is do not underestimate me.
sentence: 犬に顔を舐められました。
sentence_meaning: The dog licked my face.

mnemonic: Whatever is under it goes flat rather than into pieces. Bottles, before they go in the bin: つぶす.
notes: 壊す こわす breaks a thing so that it stops working. 潰す flattens it, and 潰れる つぶれる is it collapsing on its own.
sentence: ペットボトルは潰して捨てましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's crush plastic bottles before throwing them away.

mnemonic: You put somebody inside the count on purpose, and the ten has you in it: ふくめる.
notes: 含む ふくむ is a thing containing something. 含める is you putting it in.
sentence: 私を含めて10人が参加しました。
sentence_meaning: Ten people participated, myself included.

mnemonic: A stretch of time 時 with edges on it 期, the kind you can be in the middle of. This one matters for you: じき.
notes: 時代 じだい is an era, a historical stretch. 時期 is a season or a phase, and 際 さい is a single occasion.
sentence: 今はあなたにとって大事な時期です。
sentence_meaning: It's an important time for you now.

mnemonic: Alive 活 and moving 動, which is a good deal more than merely happening. He signed up for the local ones: かつどう.
sentence: 彼は地域の活動に参加した。
sentence_meaning: He took part in local activities.

mnemonic: A child arrives the way children arrive, and then somebody spends twenty years on it. She did that three times over: そだてる.
notes: 育つ そだつ is a child growing up. 育てる is somebody raising them.
sentence: 彼女は三人の子を育てました。
sentence_meaning: She raised three children.

mnemonic: Better 優 than the rest of them and the one ear of grain 秀 standing above the field. The best student they have: ゆうしゅう.
notes: 素晴らしい すばらしい is warm and general. 優秀 is ability measured against other people, and it goes on reports.
sentence: 彼はとても優秀な生徒です。
sentence_meaning: He's a very exceptional student.

mnemonic: You feel 感 it in advance 予 with nothing whatever to go on. He will be here in a minute, and then he is: よかん.
sentence: 彼がもうすぐ来る予感がする。
sentence_meaning: I have a feeling that he will be here soon.

mnemonic: You untie 解 the knot in the problem and the whole thing comes apart in your hands. Can you do this one: とく.
notes: 解ける とける is a problem coming undone by itself. Read ほどく the same character is untying a knot or a ribbon.
sentence: この問題を解けますか。
sentence_meaning: Can you solve this problem?

mnemonic: Back at the origin 元, and then said twice 々 for good measure. France was the plan before any of this started: もともと.
notes: 本来 ほんらい is what a thing essentially is. 元々 is what it was at the beginning.
sentence: 彼女は元々フランスに行くつもりだったの。
sentence_meaning: She was planning to go to France originally.

mnemonic: The dish was full already and now the floor has the rest of it. You left the bath running: あふれる.
sentence: バスタブからお湯が溢れました。
sentence_meaning: Hot water overflowed from the bathtub.

mnemonic: Something goes off 発 and comes into being 生 where a moment ago there was nothing. An accident, at the crossing: はっせい.
sentence: 交差点で事故が発生した。
sentence_meaning: There was an accident at the intersection.

mnemonic: A step too small to see 微 and something half a shade off 妙, and where he stands in that company is exactly that: びみょう.
notes: In speech びみょう is often a polite no. Asked how something was, it means not great.
sentence: 彼は会社で微妙な立場にあります。
sentence_meaning: He's in an iffy position in the company.

mnemonic: Two sets of feet going opposite ways 違 round the same thing, and the gap left between them is the word. These two are nowhere near: ちがい.
notes: 間違い まちがい is a mistake, a difference from what is right. 違い is a difference between two things, and 差 さ is the measurable gap.
sentence: この二つには大きな違いがある。
sentence_meaning: There's a big difference between these two.

mnemonic: Straight 直 after 後 with nothing at all in between the two. Do not lie down having only just eaten: ちょくご.
sentence: 食べた直後に寝ないほうがいいよ。
sentence_meaning: You should not sleep immediately after having eaten.

mnemonic: Under 下 the ground 地, which is where they have put the studio. Down the stairs and keep going: ちか.
sentence: スタジオは地下にあります。
sentence_meaning: The studio is in the basement.

mnemonic: Grain 禾 warming in the sun 日 and the smell of it lifting off. This flower is doing the same: かおり.
notes: 匂い におい is any smell, good or bad. 香り is a good one, and it is the word for perfume.
sentence: この花はいい香りがしますね。
sentence_meaning: This flower smells good.

mnemonic: Power 力 that actually crosses over 交 into the thing and does something there. This medicine is not managing it: きく.
notes: Same reading as 聞く きく, to hear and to ask. 効く is a thing having its effect, medicine or a brake.
sentence: この薬はあまりよく効かないよ。
sentence_meaning: This medicine doesn't work very well.

mnemonic: Two characters for using it stacked one on the other, which is what makes it the formal word. Read the manual first: しよう.
notes: 使う つかう is the everyday verb and 利用 りよう is making use of a service. 使用 is the formal noun, the one on signs and manuals.
sentence: この製品を使用する前に、説明書をお読みください。
sentence_meaning: Please read the manual before using this product.

mnemonic: The gear 具 that goes along with the way 道 you do a thing. Have we got the whole lot out: どうぐ.
sentence: 道具は全部揃っていますか。
sentence_meaning: Do we have all the tools ready?

mnemonic: The head 頁 bowed over the same plain 原 request, except this one is on behalf of everybody. World peace: ねがい.
notes: お願い おねがい is a favour you ask of a person. 願い is the wish itself.
sentence: 世界の平和が私たちの願いです。
sentence_meaning: Our wish is for world peace.

mnemonic: Water 氵 goes on first 先 and everything else comes off after it. Your face, and be quick: あらう.
sentence: 早く顔を洗いなさい。
sentence_meaning: Hurry up and wash your face.

mnemonic: The hand 手 you use and the step 段 you take to get there, and he was not fussy about either of them. Whatever it took: しゅだん.
notes: 方法 ほうほう is a method, the way a thing is done. 手段 is the means used to reach an end, often with a hint of the end justifying them.
sentence: 彼は目的のためには手段を選ばなかったわね。
sentence_meaning: He did whatever it took to achieve his goals.

mnemonic: Speech that came out wrong 誤 and got untied 解 into something else entirely at the far end. That is not what I feel: ごかい.
notes: 間違い まちがい is a plain mistake. 誤解 is taking a thing the wrong way round.
sentence: 私の気持ちを誤解しているんじゃない！
sentence_meaning: Aren't you misunderstanding my feelings?

mnemonic: You answer 応 and you put a hand out 援, from the stands and at the top of your voice. My team, every week: おうえん.
sentence: 好きなチームを応援します。
sentence_meaning: I'm cheering for the team I like.

mnemonic: Something held in the mouth 口 rather than swallowed down, and that food has more in it than the label admits: ふくむ.
notes: 含める ふくめる is you putting something in. 含む is the thing already containing it.
sentence: その食品は有害物質を含んでいるぞ。
sentence_meaning: That food contains a poisonous substance.

meaning: at that time, at the present time
mnemonic: That 当 particular time 時 rather than this one, and back then she was three years old: とうじ.
sentence: 彼女は当時、まだ3才だった。
sentence_meaning: She was only three years old at the time.

mnemonic: The win 勝 and everything that comes of it 利, which is why the entire bench is on its feet: しょうり.
sentence: チームの全員が勝利を喜んだ。
sentence_meaning: All members of the team were pleased with the victory.

mnemonic: Everything comes off the hillside 阝 at once and lands on whoever is underneath. It will do that today: ふる.
notes: Same reading as 振る ふる, to wave or shake. 降る is what rain and snow do, and 降りる おりる is getting off a train. 落ちる おちる is a thing dropping, 下がる さがる is a level coming down, and 秋 あき is the other fall, the season.
sentence: 今日、雨が降ります。
sentence_meaning: Today, it will rain.

mnemonic: Rain 雨 that turns up solid and has to be swept off the path rather than waited out. At Christmas, that year: ゆき.
sentence: クリスマスに雪が降りました。
sentence_meaning: It snowed at Christmas.

mnemonic: The mouth 口 you go in 入 by, which is exactly how the word is put together. Over that way: いりぐち.
sentence: 入り口は向こうです。
sentence_meaning: The entrance is over there.

mnemonic: One 一 direction 方 and no other one, and the sign at the end of this street means it: いっぽう.
notes: Also does on the other hand as a connector, 一方で.
sentence: ここは一方通行です。
sentence_meaning: This is a one-way street.

mnemonic: Ten mouths have passed it down and the thing is still going. He likes cars that way: ふるい.
notes: Used of things rather than of people. Calling a person 古い is not a compliment.
sentence: 私は古い車が好きです。
sentence_meaning: I like old cars.

meaning: to be useful, to be helpful
mnemonic: The thing stands up 立 in the role 役 you handed it rather than sitting there. This book earns its shelf: やくにたつ.
sentence: この本はとても役に立ちます。
sentence_meaning: This book is very useful.
